biography.plain_text: Olav V was King of Norway from 1957 to 1991, succeeding his father, Haakon VII. Born in England and raised in Norway, he trained at the Norwegian Military Academy and studied at Oxford. During the Second World War, he served the government in exile and became Norway's chief of defence in 1944.

long_biography.plain_text:
In December 1973, King Olav V took the tram to go skiing while Norway restricted driving during the oil crisis. Photographers accompanied the journey, and the image of him offering a banknote for his fare became an enduring expression of his reputation as the people's king.

Sport was a substantial part of his life. He won Olympic sailing gold at Amsterdam in 1928, returning home secretly engaged to Princess Märtha of Sweden. He later chaired the Royal Norwegian Sailing Association and served as a judge and technical expert at competitions. He also represented Norway in international sailing organisations.
